meta.about: All figures shown on the Jain labour dashboard. Edit values here; index.html reads this file.

labelDefinitions.Direct: From a named source, measuring exactly what the dashboard shows.
labelDefinitions.Proxy: From a named source, but measuring a related population, place or product.
labelDefinitions.Estimate: Projected, derived, modelled or a judgement — or the source is not recorded yet.

meta.footerSources: Sources: US Census Bureau (2022 Economic Census), BLS OES, BLS QCEW, BLS PPI, SEIU 32BJ, BSCAI, Aspire, National Immigration Forum, Operator surveys, Sproutmation, Tennant, Avidbots, Kärcher, SoftBank Robotics America, Grand View Research · May 2026; market size and machine prices updated November 2026

insight.fleetHtml: A BSC that builds a fleet of 3–5 autonomous scrubbers across their contract portfolio creates a compounding competitive advantage. The machine cost is fixed. The labour cost it replaces grows at 5.0%/yr. Every year the machine operates, the margin advantage widens.

fleetFigures.source: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS), SOC 37-2011 Janitors and Cleaners — derived
fleetFigures.label: Proxy
fleetFigures.note: Average yearly rise in the BLS median, $13.19 (2019) to $17.71 (2025) = 5.03% a year. Latest single year (2024–25): +2.5%.

insight.watchHtml: SoftBank Robotics America launched SoftBank Robotics Connect in June 2025 — a fleet management platform giving BSCs visibility across heterogeneous machine fleets from a single dashboard. Their Flagship Facility Services partnership deployed ~100 machines across 15 locations in six months. Connect tracks robot performance and cleaning SOP compliance. This is adjacent to Jain's bid intelligence layer — approaching the same problem from the machine side rather than the labour economics side. Worth monitoring as a potential integration partner or distribution channel.

compression.title: Labour Compression: Wages vs Contract Prices
compression.subtitle: Indexed, 2019 = 100 · BLS median janitor wage vs BLS producer price index for janitorial services
compression.about: Wages come from the wage chart series (BLS OEWS, May of each year). Prices are annual averages of the monthly BLS producer price index for contract janitorial services, which tracks what cleaning firms charge.
compression.takeaway: Since 2019, janitor wages are up 34% while janitorial service prices are up 21% — labour costs have outrun what BSCs can charge. The gap narrowed in 2024–25, when prices rose faster than wages.
